_comment: Wall-clock instant the fixtures under tests/golden/*.json were captured (or
shortly after they were captured) via server/scripts/capture-golden.ts.
Derivation: tests/golden/landlord-application.json's createdAt/updatedAt
fields (Postgres rows left to Prisma's `now()` default -- see
server/src/seeds/seed-postgres.ts's module docstring) read
2026-08-30T07:52:52.785Z, and a corpus-wide grep of tests/golden/*.json for
'2026-08-30' turns up the same seed-run cluster (~07:52:52.5xx-.8xx across
admin/billing/contract/inventory/tenancy/ticket/etc.) plus a second, later
cluster (08:07:09-08:21:26) on Profile rows that were touched again after
the seed run -- consistent with the capture script's own sequential
requests (tokenForEmail() signing in all 9 seeded roles, then ~25 domain
captures against a Postgres instance in ap-southeast-1) each taking real
network time. The latest timestamp found anywhere in the corpus is
capturedAt is deliberately set to the end of that same calendar day
(2026-08-30T23:59:59.999Z) rather than to any one of those exact
timestamps: erring slightly LATE relative to the true capture window is
safe (the fixtures' reports/windows are keyed off year+month, not the
exact day -- see historicalTrend/monthlyForecast in report.json and
period.start/end in inventory.json, none of which are sensitive to which
day within August 30-31 'now' falls on), whereas erring EARLY risks
landing before a real write this file is trying to postdate. Capturing at
the literal moment of the last request would be more precise but adds
restart-order fragility for no real benefit here.
Consumed by tests/contract/replay.test.ts, which freezes `Date` (via
Jest's modern fake timers, `Date` only -- see that file for why) to this
instant for the duration of the golden-fixture replay suite, so the two
cases whose response bodies are a rolling window relative to `now`
(checkout-forecast-landlord1's monthlyForecast/historicalTrend and
inventory-monthly-report-landlord1's default month/year/period) reproduce
the exact months the fixtures were captured against, rather than drifting
by one month at every real-world month boundary.
This file lives OUTSIDE tests/golden/ on purpose: replay.test.ts's fixture
discovery loop globs *.json directly under tests/golden/ and fails loudly
if that count looks wrong (see its 'discovers a plausible number of
cases' test) -- a metadata file inside that directory would silently
inflate the fixture count instead of being treated as a 26th case file.
server/scripts/capture-golden.ts overwrites this file on every re-capture
run (after its own catastrophe-guard passes, alongside the fixture
files), using the real wall-clock instant recorded at the END of that
run -- so a future re-capture keeps this frozen instant honest
automatically instead of drifting silently again.
